A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same E3VQA benchmark and M3CoT method. Their main text, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of LVLMs and prompting methods on E3VQA, including category accuracies, perspective ablations, filtering analyses, and iteration experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds LEMMA evaluations, text-only controls, temporal-misalignment analysis, scene-graph quality measurements, and computational-cost results.

M1.justification: The three scene-graph perspectives, iterative information exchange, majority voting, and fallback response are unchanged. Corresponding appendix prompts retain their procedures, with only grammatical edits. Expanded annotation and filtering descriptions do not establish a changed construction algorithm.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates data derived from Ego-Exo4D; LEMMA appears only in related work. v2 constructs and evaluates an additional 500-question LEMMA extension covering home activities and rectangular, rectified egocentric images (Appendix C.1, Table 7). It also examines temporally misaligned image pairs, extending coverage beyond synchronized inputs.

E2.justification: The principal DDCoT, CoCoT, and CCoT comparator set remains unchanged. However, v2 Table 9 newly compares these methods across Any/Ego/Exo/Both subsets, supplementing the earlier subset comparison of the default model, M3CoT, and its individual perspectives.

E3.justification: New experimental designs include 500 LEMMA questions, 80 examples assessed under 1–3-second synchronization offsets, and 120 examples evaluated for scene-graph FDR and answer accuracy. v2 also introduces text-only model evaluation and token/latency measurements. These additions substantially expand the evaluation protocol while retaining the original model settings and refinement-iteration setting.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of linguistic shortcuts, temporal-misalignment sensitivity, scene-graph quality before and after refinement, and computational cost. Figures 14–15 add conflict-resolution and failure cases, including erroneous information spreading during refinement. The original filtering, perspective, iteration, and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state that evaluations use three independent runs and report means and standard deviations. Retained result tables preserve their uncertainty reporting. The added analyses introduce no new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or statistical estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the open-source results in v1 Table 6/v2 Table 8 retain their values. v2 adds substantial results, including LEMMA M3CoT accuracies of 60.19% and 56.03%, temporal-offset label retention of 99%/97%/94%, refinement FDR decreasing from 9.37% to 6.21%, and text-only, subset, and cost results. New Table 10 reverses Gemini DDCoT/CoCoT accuracies relative to Table 2.

T1.justification: The method notation and procedural reasoning are retained, with no added or revised formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations. The new FDR and answer-accuracy descriptions provide operational criteria for empirical evaluation.

C1.justification: The benchmark, training-free method, and headline overall improvements remain the same. A limited quantitative claim changes: the introduction replaces the single 8.93% numerical-reasoning gain with 6.88% and 8.13% for GPT-4o and Gemini. The latter does not match the 7.80-percentage-point difference implied by Table 2.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning generalization beyond dataset-specific visual properties, ground-truth stability under temporal offsets, and refinement improving graph correctness and usefulness. It documents specific failure mechanisms and qualifies API latency measurements. Section 5.1 also corrects the filtered subset's description from passing screening to being removed. Most original general limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly provides a repository link and states that the dataset and source code are available. Appendix A.3 identifies annotators as authors and documents additional screening criteria; Table 10 supplies token usage and inference times. Hardware, default generation settings, model architecture information, and substantive prompt templates were already documented.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations on multimodal modeling and scene-graph evaluation, including Panoptic Scene Graph Generation and Multiview Scene Graph, and replaces some introductory/model references. The central ego-exo and VQA positioning remains stable. Much of Section 6, including the CoT overview, relocates material already present in v1's appendices.

P1.justification: The narrative is extensively reorganized: related work and the CoT overview move into main-text Section 6, single/multi-view analysis becomes Section 5.2, and appendix material is regrouped into benchmark details, evaluation settings, quantitative analyses, and qualitative examples. Widespread prose editing clarifies descriptions and cross-references.

P2.justification: v2 adds tables for text-only performance, LEMMA evaluation, comparative view-subset results, and computational cost, plus conflict-resolution and failure-case figures. Existing qualitative figures are reordered, and appendix figures, tables, and prompt boxes are reflowed. Most main-text graphics and existing table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence that was missing in v1: evaluation beyond Ego-Exo4D, direct measurements of scene-graph refinement, and quantified computational costs. Text-only controls, temporal checks, and failure cases also make applicability and weaknesses easier to assess. These gains outweigh localized reporting errors, notably the unsupported 8.13% Gemini numerical gain and the DDCoT/CoCoT accuracy swap in Table 10; the retained principal results remain unchanged.
